text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Hizbollah intends to step up attacks in south Lebanon, Iran increases aid to group.
- Yigal Amir's friend Margalit Har-Shefi to go on trial on charges of involvement in Rabin assassination.
- All Palestinian women prisoners arrested before Israel-PLO peace deal was signed in 1993 will be released today.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu says he will raise during Washington visit need to find bridging formula for resuming peace talks with Syria.
- Foreign airlines reject Israeli Chief Rabbinate demand to serve only kosher food on flights from Israel.
- Parliament's finance committee approves sale of 20 percent of state's stake in Israel Chemicals to Shoul Eisenberg.
- Since start of 1997, Intel has presented three plans to Israeli Investment Authority to invest $182 million in Israel.
- Institutional stage of Israel Discount Bank public offering closes 0.6 percent above minimum price.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu trying to avoid U.S. extradition of suspected Hamas leader Abu Marzook, fearing terror attacks after his handover.
- El Al to lose between $20 million and $40 million in 1997, according to sources in the airline.
MAARIV
- 79 percent of the public oppose unilateral Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon.
- Two tracker dogs among casualties in Israeli helicopter crash.
- MI Holdings publishes tender for underwriters of Bank Leumi public offering.
GLOBES
- Claridge Israel president says it contending again for Bank Hapoalim because of massive change in its view of Israeli economic and political situation.
- Israel Discount Bank economists say additional budget cut will be needed through taxation and rise in the price of services.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister Netanyahu to reveal final-status principles to U.S. President Clinton.
- Third Way, National Religious Party threaten to topple government over Jerusalem construction.
- Court: No way to block Palestinian women prisoner release.
